definition.text: unique human-readable identifier of a SIF typical
human-readable name of a safety instrumented function (SIF) typical
description of the design intent of the SIF
state of the process  when safety is achieved
specifies whether the safety instrumented function (SIF) is a local SIF or a global SIF

way in which a safety-related system is intended to be used, with respect to the frequency of demands made upon it, which may be either low demand mode, where the frequency of demands for operation made on a safety related, system is no greater than one per year and no greater than twice the proof-test, frequency; or high demand or continuous mode, where the frequency of demands for operation made, on a safety-related system is greater than one per year or greater than twice the proof check frequency
occurrence in a production process which initiates a reaction of a technical system
reaction of a technical system to a cause
method applied for allocating SIL requirement to a SIF
method and/or tool used for quantification of probability of failure on demand (PFD), probability of failure per hour (PFH) and/or the common cause failure (CCF)
reference to or description of barrier that the safety instrumented function or part of the safety instrumented system represents
unique human-readable identifier of a safety instrumented function (SIF)
human-readable name of a safety instrumented function (SIF)
reference to a regulatory document that is connected to the SIF
alphanumeric character sequence uniquely identifying a document version
required level (one out of four) of a safety instrumented function (SIF) for the safety integrity of the safety instrumented system (SIS)
required level (one out of four) allocated to the safety instrumented function (SIF) for specifying the environmental integrity requirement to be achieved by the safety instrumented system (SIS)
required level (one out of four) of a safety instrumented function (SIF) for specifying the asset integrity of the safety instrumented system (SIS)

process operating mode, any planned state of process operation, including modes such as start-up after emergency shutdown, normal start-up, operation, temporary operation, emergency operation and shutdown.
maximum allowable (average) Probability of dangerous failure on demand (PFD)
maximum allowable average frequency of dangerous failure (failures per hour)
origin of the demand (why it occurred)

requirement for being able to manually bring the process to a safe state
specific action or intervention designed to reduce the probability of common cause failures
factor in the planning/design process that is considered to be true, real, or certain, without proof or demonstration
properties characterizing a requirement
source of the requirement under consideration
alphanumeric character sequence uniquely identifying a measuring or control point
plain text characterizing a process control engineering request

period of time between a failure occurring in the process or the basic process control system (with the potential to give rise to a hazardous event) and the occurrence of the hazardous event if the SIF is not performed
textual description of the hazardous event, i.e. an event that can cause harm
identifier of a hazardous event
hazard that is due to a dangerous combination of output states of the safety instrumented system (SIS)
specific action or intentionally designed measure to reduce the probability of a hazard from combined safe process state
any independent mechanism that reduces risk by control, prevention or mitigation
number of devices within an input device group, logic solver group, or final element group
"M" in a "MooN" system that is functioning if at least M out of its N redundant channels are functioning
total number of input device groups, logic solver groups and final element groups specified for a safety instrumented function (SIF)

mathematical equation reflecting the configuration of the Reliability block diagram (RBD) and the associated probability of failure (or success), if A and B are devices (or groups of devices) in series in the RBD it can be expressed as A+B, and if A and B are redundant devices (or groups of devices) of the RBD it can be expressed as A*B.
actual experienced demand rate (number of true demands per year) for a certain SIF or SIS device
number of demands experienced for a safety instrumented function (SIF) during operation
number of experienced spurious trips per year for a safety instrumented function or a SIS device
number of spurious trips experienced for a certain SIF or SIS device
mark attributed to an instant by means of a specified timescale, expressed as a date and a time
brief description of the demand, i.e. how/why the SIF or the SIS device was activated
time period between when a process reached the SIF activation set point and the SIF final elements completed the necessary actions to achieve the process safe state
number of performed tests of a certain type
number of failed tests experienced for a considered SIS device or group of SIS devices
the physical location where the test is performed
result of performed proof test with respect to if it has failed or passed according to the fail criterion
actual measured value upon a performed proof test
description of the result of a performed test
any comment to a performed loop test or proof test
average probatbility of failure on demand (see IEC 61508-4) based on operational failure data
average probability of failure per hour based on operational experience for a safety instrumented function, a SIS component, or a group of SIS components

certain requirements to persons involved in the life cycle of the SIF, which are requested when the SIF depend on legal requirements

assumptions generic for all SIFs on the plant
requirements generic for all SIFs on the plant

event that can cause harm

group of input devices

group of logic solver devices
group of final elements
voting MooN between groups of devices within a safety instrumented function (SIF)

logical diagram made up of functional blocks that are depicted as rectangles or squares and connected by lines, and has a single starting point and a single end point, and where each block in the diagram represents a device and the arrangement of blocks (series, parallel, or combinations) reflects how failures or correct functions of the devices impact the safety instrumented function as a whole.
data characterizing the occurrence of a demand
occurrence of a demand on a safety instrumented function (SIF)

occurrence of a loop test

foundational engineering document that outlines the key technical criteria, design assumptions, constraints, and standards that guide the development of a system, facility, or project
set of written guidelines or instructions for the completion of a routine task, designed to increase performance, improve efficiency, and ensure quality through systemic homogenization

hazard and operability study, a structured and systematic method for examining a process or operation to identify possible hazards and operating problems, especially by considering deviations from the intended design or function

layer of protection analysis, a structured risk assessment method used to evaluate whether existing or proposed independent protection layers are sufficient to reduce a hazardous scenario to an acceptable level of risk
document representing the graphical and logical representation of a SIF made up of lines and functional blocks
